rawItems.title: Ramsey builder named Builder of the Year for Midlands and Wales
rawItems.content: A Ramsey builder has been named Builder of the Year at the Checkatrade Regional Awards. Liam Hilbrown of Carter’s Restoration Services received the honour for the Midlands and Wales region at a ceremony held earlier this month at the Wolverhampton Wanderers Stadium. The awards celebrate tradespeople who demonstrate not only exceptional craftsmanship but also professionalism and reliability. Jambu Palaniappan, CEO of Checkatrade, said: "Great trades earn their place on Checkatrade and keep earning it. "But members like Liam Hilbrown go a step beyond this already high bar. "The Checkatrade Awards are all about celebrating the pride and effort our outstanding members put into their work, and shining a light on their achievements. "We’re very proud of them all." Winners are chosen from more than 2,500 nominations nationwide. Checkatrade sets a rigorous entry standard for its members, requiring up to 12 checks before joining and ongoing monitoring through customer feedback. The awards will conclude with a national final in London on November 19, where regional winners will compete for national honours.

McMorris scored twice during the second half to complete his hat-trick and secure the win. The Women’s 1s defeated Cambridge South 2s 2-0. Belle Holmes opened the scoring in the 16th minute, while Kira Herbert added the second goal during the second half. St Neots also kept a clean sheet. The Men’s 2s drew 2-2 away to Cambridge South 4s. Sami Farrer equalised after receiving an aerial assist from Iain Moor. Cambridge South regained the lead before half-time. St Neots continued to create pressure and Henry Milner scored from a short corner late in the match to earn a point. The Men’s 3s drew 1-1 with Newmarket 3s. Newmarket scored shortly after half-time, but Sam Douglas equalised late in the match. The Men’s 4s secured a 1-0 win against Kettering 5s. Eddie Penrose scored in the 11th minute, with the goal proving enough to secure the points. The Women’s 2s lost 4-3 away to Haverhill. Councillors have voted to refuse a controversial 199-home development plan for Ramsey despite receiving a recommendation for approval. BDW Trading Ltd submitted the proposal for land south of The Malting with landowners Susan and Robert Pickard. The scheme included up to 199 homes, 40 per cent affordable housing, children’s play areas, drainage infrastructure and related works. Developers also proposed a landscaped perimeter, a 1.1km circular walking route linked to public rights of way and green infrastructure covering around 37 per cent of the site. The site is land south of The Malting in Ramsey However, at a meeting on October 19, Huntingdonshire District Council's Development Management Committee voted to refuse the outline application, which had been recommended for approval. Planning officers said the benefits outweighed the harm, pointing to Huntingdonshire’s current shortfall in five-year housing land supply. The report said the scheme would help meet housing need and provide substantial affordable housing. Cllr Andrew Wood proposed refusing the plan against officers’ recommendation, subject to consultation with the Secretary of State. items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Planning Minutes (Agenda - Planning Meeting 24 Sept 2026): Unanimously recommended refusal for outline application 26/00142/OUT on grounds of highway safety on Oilmills Road, surface water flood risk, and overdevelopment beyond the settlement boundary.

items.title: Planning Committee Approves High Street Commercial Refurbishment & Signage
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Planning Minutes (Agenda - Planning Meeting 24 Sept 2026): Supported planning application 26/00188/FUL for commercial shopfront renovation and heritage signage in the Ramsey Conservation Area.

items.title: Great Whyte Pedestrian Safety & Speed Limit Review
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Minutes (Agenda Full Council 10 September 2026): Council resolved to submit a formal request to Cambridgeshire County Council Highways for a 20mph speed zone and upgraded zebra crossing along Great Whyte, following resident traffic survey feedback.
items.documentTitle: Ramsey Town Council - Full Council Agenda 20260910

items.title: Town Council Approves Drainage Repairs & New Play Equipment for Spinningfield
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Amenities Committee (Agenda Full Council 10 September 2026): Approved £14,500 contract for drainage improvements across Spinningfield recreation ground, alongside installation of replacement inclusive swing sets in September.
